subject: Climate & Environment
title: The History of Solar Energy
description: One-minute skill: The History of Solar Energy.

hook.text: In 1954, Bell Labs built the first practical solar cell. It powered a small toy Ferris wheel.

buildup.text: Early cells converted just 6% of sunlight. They cost $1,000 per watt — absurdly expensive.

discovery.text: NASA became the first big customer, putting solar panels on satellites in the 1960s.

twist.text: The oil crisis of 1973 sparked interest in solar for homes — then oil prices dropped and so did funding.

climax.text: Solar costs fell 99% since 1976. It is now the cheapest electricity source in history.

punchline.text: From a toy Ferris wheel to the cheapest power on Earth.

quiz.question: When was the first practical solar cell built?

details.summary: The photovoltaic effect was discovered in 1839 by Edmond Becquerel, but practical solar cells only emerged in the 1950s at Bell Labs. Costs have fallen over 99 percent since then, transforming solar from a space-program novelty into the world's fastest-growing energy source.
details.whyItMatters: Solar's dramatic cost decline shows how sustained investment in technology can transform energy systems. Its history offers lessons for developing other clean technologies.
takeaways: The photovoltaic effect was discovered in 1839
Bell Labs built the first practical silicon cell in 1954
Solar panel costs have fallen over 99 percent since the 1970s

faq.question: Why did solar panels become so cheap?
faq.answer: Government subsidies in Germany, Japan, and China stimulated mass production. Manufacturing scale, improved efficiency, and fierce competition drove a learning curve where each doubling of production cut costs by about 20 percent.

faq.question: When did solar become competitive with fossil fuels?
faq.answer: Solar reached grid parity in sunny regions around 2015 and is now the cheapest new electricity source in countries receiving more than two-thirds of the world's sunlight. Costs continue falling, widening its competitive advantage.
